curiosities: It was designed at Epyx as the 'Handy' by RJ Mical and Dave Needle, then sold to Atari.
It was the first handheld console with a colour LCD.
The picture can be flipped so left-handed players can hold it upside down.
Up to eight Lynxes can be linked with ComLynx cables in some games.
Its two custom chips are named Mikey and Suzy.
Its screen is 160 × 102 pixels, its colours from 4,096.
It scales sprites in hardware, which few consoles of its time could.
Six AA batteries lasted about four to five hours.
The smaller Lynx II of 1991 runs longer on its batteries.
